transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-10-29 15:00 UTC — Duration 46 minutes
Attendees: Alyssa Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus Patel (Redwood SE), Riley Gomez (Redwood CSM); Priya Nair (SummitWare Head of Platform), Tom Kovac (Director ML Infra), Sandra Lee (Security & Compliance), Jamal Ortiz (Procurement)

Summary: Quick renewal check, SummitWare wants to increase retainer and add EU edge region + private VPC for data residency. Security asks (SOC2 evidence, KMS, audit logs). Agreement in-principle on extension; need pricing + bench + procurement timeline.

Topics: retainer uplift, region onboarding (eu-west), private VPC deployment path, SLA/latency targets, cost vs latency tradeoffs, compliance artifacts, next steps and timing.

[00:00] Alyssa: Hey everyone thanks for doing this, uh we can go 45 minutes, real quick agenda — retainer ask, eu region, private — any immediate blockers?
[00:12] Priya: Thanks Alyssa. We're on a tight timeline, end of quarter budgeting so would like to lock numbers and PO by mid-November if possible. main ask is add eu-west region and bump retainer 40%. Also want to understand private VPC path and how quickly we can get a staging cluster.
[00:32] Marcus: Great, quick clarifying q; when you say eu-west do you want Redwood hosted region or a private onprem / VPC deployment in eu?
[00:44] Tom: Prefer managed (hosted) for the start but need data residency so either dedicated eu-hosted or private VPC in eu cloud — leaning dedicated/dedicated pool rather than fully on-prem.
[01:02] Alyssa: Perfect. Pricing note — a retainer uplift to cover steady-state throughput plus burst buffer. we'll send a new pricing matrix. The 40% bump headline is doable but we'll need to map to tokens/day and burst percent.
[01:24] Sandra: On compliance — we need SOC2 Type II, ISO27001 artifacts, and KMS integration details. encryption in transit and at rest are musts. also audit log retention and proof of key separation.
[01:38] Marcus: Yep we can share SOC2 pack + our security whitepaper. small caveat on KMS — for private deployments we integrate customer KMS via RPC; for hosted we offer envelope encryption with customer-managed keys in supported clouds. 
[01:57] Tom: How does that affect latency? our SLO needs p95 < 200 ms for short responses, and p99 under 500 ms for longer seqs, realistically for our top-level inference path.
[02:15] Marcus: If you go dedicated in eu region we can meet p95 ~ 120-150 ms for short gen at 50 RPS with our optimized runtime. p99 on longer contexts depends on batching and quantization choices. There's a tradeoff: more quantization lowers cost but can add variance for p99 on complex prompts.
[02:41] Priya: Okay, so we need proposals for two scenarios: (1) hosted dedicated eu pool with KMS/customer keys envelope, (2) private VPC in our cloud with customer KMS and separate SLAs. both with pricing + timeline.
[02:58] Alyssa: we'll do both. also Marcus will run a benchmark with your sample workload. Jamal, procurement? timeline yes/no?
[03:08] Jamal: If pricing lands by next Wednesday we can get PO signed by Nov 18 latest. need final SOW and pricing table. also please include cancellation terms and renewal cadence.
[03:21] Alyssa: noted. we'll include SOW and a term sheet.
[03:25] [silence / typing] 
[03:38] Marcus: Quick technical note — for your highest throughput routes we recommend pinned model versions and a reserved GPU pool. that avoids cold starts and KV cache misses. our autoscaler can still burst but the reserved pool ensures steady latency.
[03:55] Tom: Pinned model versions could add cost. how does caching reduce token spend? we currently use prefix caching for a FAQ flow so reuse is high.
[04:07] Marcus: Prefix/KV cache reduces token compute and overall per-token cost; depends on reuse rate. we'll quantify in the benchmark. also, for your longer sequences 8k context we recommend q4 quantization profile on A100-like instances if you go private to balance mem and accuracy.
[04:28] Priya: You mentioned q4? We've seen model quality degrade in some edge cases. Need quality numbers vs cost.
[04:35] Marcus: Agreed — metric we'll report: ROUGE-like for your prompt set and a small human-blind eval for top intents. we'll surface delta vs fp16 baseline.
[04:50] Sandra: On audit logs — we need logs forwarded to our SIEM and retention 7 years. Is that supported?
[05:00] Riley: Yes, audit logs can be forwarded via syslog/S3 to your bucket; retention configurable for private deployments. hosted has retention tiers — we can propose a paid longer retention add-on.
[05:15] Priya: Great. also, any network egress considerations for eu region? cost estimates?
[05:22] Alyssa: We'll add egress estimates in the pricing matrix — depends on model outputs and token volumes.
[05:28] [short crosstalk] 
[05:35] Marcus: About provisioning timing — for a dedicated eu pool we can provision in 2-3 weeks once capacity is reserved. For private VPC in your cloud, depends on networking approvals but usually 4-6 weeks end-to-end.
[05:51] Tom: So if we sign by Nov 18, in prod eu region by mid-December is possible?
[05:58] Marcus: Yes, mid-Dec seems achievable for dedicated; private VPC might slip into late Dec/Jan depending on approvals.
[06:08] Jamal: Are there any long lead hardware constraints? we need guaranteed capacity not just soft-commit.
[06:15] Alyssa: For committed capacity we do reserved capacity contracts — that locks pool size and gives SLA. that's part of the SOW pricing options.
[06:24] Priya: On SLAs — can you share historical NOC uptime and p99 latency histograms?
[06:32] Riley: We'll attach per-model latency histograms and NOC uptime summary.
[06:38] Sandra: One security question: can we bring our HSM for key wrapping in a private deployment?
[06:44] Marcus: Yes, for private VPC or on-prem we have integrations for customer HSMs. hosted customer-managed key integrations are limited to cloud KMS variants; full HSM plug-ins are for private/on-prem.
[07:00] Tom: For the benchmark — we'll give you a representative set: 60% short chat requests, 30% semantically heavy completions, 10% embeddings hybrid. want to confirm the sample size and sequence lengths.
[07:12] Marcus: Send us a sample CSV and expected RPS; we'll run at a 100 RPS profile for headroom and also a 20 RPS baseline. we'll dump p95/p99 and cost per 1M tokens.
[07:26] Priya: Good. the question about model fallback — if you have a lighter quantized model for failover, does Redwood automatically route?
[07:35] Marcus: We have smart routing rules; can fallback to compatible variants — we can set priority to preserve latency SLOs and fail open/closed behavior. We'll provide recommended policies.
[07:48] Jamal: Any procurement risks? price increase mid-term?
[07:53] Alyssa: We'll propose fixed pricing for 12 months on the reserved bundle. add-on usage billed monthly. term negotiation can include price protection clauses.
[08:04] [laughter] 
[08:12] Priya: A couple more security items — pen tests, vulnerability disclosure program, and support SLA for incident response. Sandra will specify exact RTOs.
[08:23] Sandra: We want 24/7 pager escalation for Sev1 and 4 hour initial ack. can you commit?
[08:31] Riley: Standard Sev1 is 1 hour initial ack, on-call rotation. 4 hour ack can be included in an enterprise support tier — we'll include that option in the SOW.
[08:45] Tom: Let's talk cost buckets quickly: reserved capacity, burst buffer, storage for KV cache, logs retention. can you give ballpark % split?
[08:56] Marcus: Ballpark: reserved capacity ~70% of monthly bill for steady state, burst ~15%, storage/logs ~10%, support/compliance addons ~5% — rough estimate, will refine in pricing.
[09:14] Priya: Okay. on the EU localization — need public endpoints inside eu and certs for data processing addendum.
[09:22] Alyssa: We'll include DPA and the data flow diagram for eu-hosted.
[09:27] Jamal: Procurement will need commercial terms, PO instructions, and the redwood W-9 and bank details.
[09:34] Alyssa: I'll attach those.
[09:38] [brief pause] 
[09:46] Marcus: One more technical: For your FAQ flow, prefix caching should give large cost reductions — if reuse is 60% you can see token cost reductions of 30-40%. We'll show numbers with your sample.
[09:59] Tom: Nice. Also want to surface a rollback plan if a new model rollout regresses quality. what's your A/B rollout support?
[10:08] Marcus: We support canary and A/B, automatic fallback to prior pinned version on quality regressions, and tie-ins with Redwood Optimize for monitoring. We'll recommend a canary window and guardrails.
[10:24] Priya: Good. anything else from your side?
[10:27] Sandra: I need an answer on data residency for logs — are they separated per region?
[10:32] Riley: Yes, logs can be stored per-region for private clusters, for hosted we'll ensure EU logs remain in EU bucket. we'll document specific storage endpoints.
[10:44] Jamal: Timeline recap — pricing by next Wed, bench by Friday, procurement sign by Nov 18. provisioning kickoff week of Nov 17. is that right?
[10:56] Alyssa: Yes that's what we'll aim for.
[11:02] Marcus: I'll run the benchmark as soon as we have the sample and baseline RPS. expect initial results in 24-48 hours after run.
[11:13] Priya: Great. Last question — edge readiness for other regions later (apac) — can we use the same SOW template to add regions?
[11:21] Alyssa: Yes we'll include modular add-on clauses for additional regions.
[11:25] [typing noise] 
[11:33] Alyssa: Okay let's do a quick recap of agreed items and owners — pricing matrix & SOW (Alyssa), benchmark (Marcus), security docs (Riley + Marcus), procurement timeline (Jamal). Any final notes?
[11:47] Tom: Make sure the bench includes p99 for 8k contexts and token-cost per 1M baseline.
[11:55] Marcus: noted.
[12:00] Priya: Thanks all. We'll be waiting for the docs.
[12:05] Alyssa: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with attachments and a proposed PO-ready SOW.

Recap / Action items (auto):
- Alyssa: Pricing matrix + SOW (due 2025-11-05)
- Marcus: Benchmark runs + report (due 2025-11-07)
- Riley/Marcus: Security artifacts, SOC2 pack, KMS integration notes (due 2025-11-12)
- Jamal: Confirm procurement/PO date (due 2025-11-14)

References mentioned: pricing spreadsheet link (sent after call), SOC2 pack (redwood-docs link), benchmark script (redwood-bench repo link).

End of transcript.
